turns.answer_text:
The training set is noisy experimental zT, so I treated this as a composition-space regression problem rather than a simple nearest-neighbor lookup.

**What the data show**
- Features are atomic fractions of Sb, Co, Fe. `1 − (Sb+Co+Fe)` is the filler fraction. Stoichiometric filled skutterudites have Sb/(Co+Fe) ≈ 3.
- Unfilled CoSb3 (filler ≈ 0) is poor (zT ~ 0.2). Filler in ~0.015–0.04 with Fe = 0 is the high-zT n-type region.
- A second good family is p-type Fe on the Co site (Fe/(Fe+Co) ≈ 0.75).
- Two isolated Co-rich points (Sb ≈ 0.588, Co ≈ 0.395, zT = 1.26 and 1.32) sit off skutterudite stoichiometry but are internally consistent.

**Models**
ExtraTrees / RF / HGB / distance-weighted kNN (10-fold R² ≈ 0.32–0.34) plus multi-seed averaging and rank aggregation. All of them put the same five pool rows on top.

| rank | id | composition | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **c023** | Sb 0.587, Co 0.396, Fe 0 | essentially the two zT≈1.29 measurements; every model’s #1 |
| 2 | **c065** | Sb 0.742, Co 0.241, Fe 0 | next to zT=1.206; most stable tree rank |
| 3 | **c067** | Sb 0.722, Co 0.242, Fe 0 | nearest to the global max (zT=1.367 and 1.289); best well-populated cluster (mean ≈ 1.02, n=5) |
| 4 | **c008** | Sb 0.738, Co 0.244, Fe 0 | dense filled-CoSb3 neighborhood, 5-NN mean ≈ 1.04 |
| 5 | **c046** | Sb 0.738, Co 0.244, Fe 0 | same neighborhood as c008 |

c001 (light Fe doping) and c020 (Fe-rich p-type) are next, but clearly behind these five.

Final: c023, c065, c067, c008, c046
